To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GRK2 uses a conserved surface to dock with G protein-couple receptors, but there are subtle differences in this surface that may contribute to the selectivity of GRKs.
the extreme N-terminal helices (αN) and active site tethers (AST) of GRK2 are critical for receptor phosphorylation and recruitment to the receptor in vitro and in vivo.
GRK2 interacts with activated G protein-couple receptors via a surface of the kinase domain including the N-terminal helix and the active site tethers.

the molecular mechanisms that govern the specificity of GRKs for their substrates, and how the activation of G protein-coupling receptors by agonists is linked to the regulation of GRK activity.
